newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Permanent says growth continues.
newsitem.headline: Irish Permanent says growth continues.

text.p: Irish Permanent Plc said on Tuesday that it was experiencing continuing growth in its key business activities and had a significant share of the new mortgage lending market.
"These interim results reflect continuing growth in key business areas..., helped by a strong economy," Irish Permanent chief executive Roy Douglas said in a results statement.
Douglas said the group continued to capture a significant share of new mortgage lending in the current buoyant market.
The group reported a rise of 16.8 percent in first half pretax profit to 23.3 million punts.

Douglas said despite a competitive savings environment, retail savings inflows remained positive and the wider retail financial services now provided by the group were making a growing contribution to profitability.

Irish Permanent said the increase in first half net interest income, which rose to 48.5 million pounds from 44.5 million, was due to the continuing growth of residential mortgages and strong growth in Irish Permanent Finance, the group's car and personal loan subsidiary.

Irish Permanent said the strong performance in the first half was achieved against a background of increased competition in its core markets where underlying conditions "remain positive for the second half of 1996".

Growth in other income, which rose by more than one million punts to 8.7 million, reflected an increased contribution from Irish Progressive Group, which had earnings of 5.1 million compared to 4.5 million in for the same period last year, it said.
Provisions for bad and doubtful debts were 1.3 million compared to 1.6 million for the first half of 1995, it said.
